courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: What if we now try to edit this?
If I remove the exclamation marks and I reloaded the app whilst I was on this page,
so I have not visited offers and discover. If I now try to save this, I get an error
and the reason for that error simply is that on the places service, we have our update place method
and there, we get that data which we just entered on the form
but then we try to update a place in our array of places.
Now obviously that might not exist though, we're fetching our array of places here but initially, that
is empty right,
we initialize the behavior subject with an empty place and this only changes if fetchPlaces is called,
so if we do fetch places from our back-end but we never did this here.
So how can we work around this then?
Well in the end here in switch map where I try to get my places, we can add an if check and we can see
if not places or if places length is smaller or equal than zero, which means we don't have any places yet
and in this case the observable I want to return here is this fetchPlaces, to fetch my places with the
help of the fetchPlaces method. Remember the fetchPlaces method here in the end will go ahead and fetch
all places and it will then also update our places in the subscription but more important than that,
it will also give us the places in the subscribe method. We haven't used that thus far because we only
needed the update and the subscription,
now down here we're not interested in the subscription update because we don't set up an ongoing subscription,
we only take one snapshot and that would be the empty list here
if there are no places initially but the good thing is fetchPlaces still returns us this updated array
of places, so we can use that here too and the subscription will be changed or the global list of places
in the behavior subject will be changed along the way in the background as well
by the logic we have in fetchPlaces.
So here, I returned this fetchPlaces
if we have no places yet,
otherwise so in the else case, I just return places
but this would now be invalid because you actually need to return an observable here and for this,
rxjs has the nice auth observable creation operator which you import up there from rxjs,
so not from rxjs/operators but just from rxjs
and what auth does is it takes any value, like an array or a number, doesn't matter and it wraps it into
a new observable that will immediately emit a value and this is only required here so that in both cases,
we definitely return an observable because in switch map, you need to return one. And now you can take all
that logic here
and cut that and add another switch map
operator here where you now get your places list again
and now here you can add all the logic you had in the old switch map operator.
The difference here simply is that now places is guaranteed to be an array here because either we had
one right from the start, then this of course was a bit of a redundant step but it also doesn't hurt
or we had no places,
well then this was a super important step because then we fetched places and now with that, we make sure
that when we update our places, we should always have a list of places which we can update.
So if I now added this and removed the exclamation marks and I save this, now this looks way better
even though I never visited any other page before but our updating logic now works because we ensure
that we always have a list of places to work with.
